newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to resist pressure to open economy further.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to resist pressure to open economy further.

text.p: The Brazilian government plans to resist pressure by industrialized countries to further reduce import tariffs on industrial products in 1997, Folha de S. Paulo newspaper said.
"We cannot submit the national industry to a second liberal shock," the paper quoted Foreign Minister Luiz Felipe Lampreia as saying.

Pressure on Brazil to lower import duties is expected to come at a World Trade Organization ministerial conference Dec 9-13 in Singapore, which will review progress on meeting goals set out by the Uruguay Round, the paper said.

Lampreia said Brazil has met the requirements of the Uruguay Round, which created a mechanism for lowering trade barriers by 2000, as well as the goals of the four-nation Mercosur customs union, according to the paper.

Folha said the United States and other industrialized nations want a new round of barrier and tariff reductions, especially in information technology like semiconductors and computer software and hardware.
